blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 13 (Differentiation), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 Find, by using \(m_{\text{tan}} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\), the gradient and an equation of the tangent line to \(f(x) = x^{2} + 2x\) at \(P(1, 3)\). Show that the tangent meets the curve only at \(P\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Check \(P\) is on the curve, put \(x = 1\) in the limit, cancel \(\delta x\), then use the point-slope form.

book_ref.quote: the line touches the curve at \(P\) and does not cut it again

steps: \(f(1 + \delta x) - f(1) = 4\delta x + \delta x^{2} = \delta x(4 + \delta x)\)
\(m_{\text{tan}} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\delta x(4 + \delta x)}{\delta x} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}(4 + \delta x) = 4\)
blocks.final_answer: Gradient \(= 4\); tangent \(y = 4x - 1\), touching the curve only at \(P(1, 3)\).

blocks.prompt: 2 For \(f(x) = x^{3}\), find the average rate of change from \(x = 1\) to \(x = 1 + \delta x\). Evaluate it for \(\delta x = 0.1\) and \(\delta x = 0.01\), and find the instantaneous rate of change at \(x = 1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Average rate = difference quotient; its limit as \(\delta x \to 0\) is the instantaneous rate.

book_ref.quote: If \(x_{1}\) approaches \(x\), then

steps: \(f(1 + \delta x) - f(1) = (1 + \delta x)^{3} - 1 = 3\delta x + 3\delta x^{2} + \delta x^{3}\)
Average rate \(= \dfrac{3\delta x + 3\delta x^{2} + \delta x^{3}}{\delta x} = 3 + 3\delta x + \delta x^{2}\)
blocks.final_answer: Average rate \(3 + 3\delta x + \delta x^{2}\) (\(3.31\), \(3.0301\)); instantaneous rate at \(x = 1\) is \(3\), i.e. \(f'(1) = 3\).

blocks.prompt: 3 A particle moves along a line with position \(s(t) = 2t^{2} + 3t + 1\) metres after \(t\) seconds. Find (i) the average velocity over \([1, 4]\) and (ii) the instantaneous velocity at \(t = 2\) by the limit. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: (i) uses \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{s(t_{1}) - s(t)}{t_{1} - t}\); (ii) uses \(v_{\text{inst}} = \lim_{\delta t \to 0}\frac{s(t+\delta t) - s(t)}{\delta t}\).

book_ref.quote: the average velocity becomes the instantaneous velocity

steps: \(s(2 + \delta t) = 2(4 + 4\delta t + \delta t^{2}) + 6 + 3\delta t + 1 = 15 + 11\delta t + 2\delta t^{2}\)
\(v_{\text{inst}} = \lim_{\delta t \to 0}\dfrac{\delta t(11 + 2\delta t)}{\delta t} = \lim_{\delta t \to 0}(11 + 2\delta t) = 11\) m/sec

blocks.prompt: 4 Using \(f'(a) = \lim_{x \to a}\dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\), find the derivative of \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\) at \(x = a\) (\(a \ne 0\)). Hence find the gradient of the curve at \(x = 2\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Make one fraction on top; the factor \(x - a\) appears with a minus sign and cancels.

book_ref.quote: is called the derivative or gradient of

steps: \(\dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a} = \dfrac{a - x}{ax(x - a)} = \dfrac{-(x - a)}{ax(x - a)}\)

blocks.prompt: 5 Find from first principles the derivative of \(f(x) = x^{3} - 2x\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The four steps; expand \((x + \delta x)^{3}\).

book_ref.quote: can be found by the following four steps

steps: Step II: \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = x^{3} + 3x^{2}\delta x + 3x(\delta x)^{2} + (\delta x)^{3} - 2x - 2\delta x - x^{3} + 2x\)
Step III: \(\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = 3x^{2} + 3x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^{2} - 2\)

blocks.prompt: 6 Find from first principles the derivative of \(f(x) = \sqrt{3x + 1}\) and the gradient of its graph at \(x = 5\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Rationalize the numerator to bring out the factor \(\delta x\).

book_ref.quote: Whenever a square root appears in the numerator of the difference quotient, rationalize the numerator

steps: Step II: \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = \dfrac{(3x + 3\delta x + 1) - (3x + 1)}{\sqrt{3x + 3\delta x + 1} + \sqrt{3x + 1}} = \dfrac{3\delta x}{\sqrt{3x + 3\delta x + 1} + \sqrt{3x + 1}}\)
Step III: \(\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3x + 3\delta x + 1} + \sqrt{3x + 1}}\), \((\delta x \ne 0)\)

blocks.prompt: 7 Find by definition the derivative of \(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x + 1}\), \(x \ne -1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Take the common denominator \((x + 1)(x + \delta x + 1)\); the numerator simplifies to \(\delta x\).

book_ref.quote: With fractions, the key algebra move is taking a common denominator.

steps: Step II: \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = \dfrac{(x + \delta x)(x + 1) - x(x + \delta x + 1)}{(x + 1)(x + \delta x + 1)}\)
Numerator: \(x^{2} + x + x\,\delta x + \delta x - x^{2} - x\,\delta x - x = \delta x\), so \(f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = \dfrac{\delta x}{(x + 1)(x + \delta x + 1)}\)
Step III: \(\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{1}{(x + 1)(x + \delta x + 1)}\)

blocks.prompt: 8 If \(y = \dfrac{1}{x^{3}}\), find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) by ab-initio method and its value at \(x = -1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Common denominator, then factorize \(x^{3} - (x + \delta x)^{3}\) to bring out \(-\delta x\).

book_ref.quote: The value of \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) at \(x = -1\) is written as

steps: \(y + \delta y = \dfrac{1}{(x + \delta x)^{3}}\), so \(\delta y = \dfrac{x^{3} - (x + \delta x)^{3}}{x^{3}(x + \delta x)^{3}}\)
\(\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = \dfrac{-\left[3x^{2} + 3x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^{2}\right]}{x^{3}(x + \delta x)^{3}}\), \((\delta x \ne 0)\)

blocks.prompt: 9 Prove that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) when \(n\) is a positive integer. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: First principles with the binomial expansion of \((x + \delta x)^{n}\).

book_ref.quote: We find the derivative of \(x^{n}\) when \(n\) is positive integer.

steps: Let \(y = x^{n}\). Then \(y + \delta y = (x + \delta x)^{n}\) and \(\delta y = (x + \delta x)^{n} - x^{n}\)
Binomial theorem: \(\delta y = \left[x^{n} + nx^{n-1}\delta x + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{n-2}(\delta x)^{2} + \ldots + (\delta x)^{n}\right] - x^{n}\)
Every term except the first contains \(\delta x\), so as \(\delta x \to 0\): \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = nx^{n-1}\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) for every positive integer \(n\).

blocks.prompt: 10 Prove that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) when \(n\) is a negative integer (\(x \ne 0\)). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Put \(n = -m\) with \(m\) a positive integer, so \(y = \frac{1}{x^{m}}\); expand \((x + \delta x)^{m}\) in the numerator.

book_ref.quote: Let \(n = -m\) (\(m\) is a positive integer)

steps: By the binomial theorem \(x^{m} - (x + \delta x)^{m} = -\delta x\left[mx^{m-1} + \dfrac{m(m-1)}{2!}x^{m-2}\delta x + \ldots + (\delta x)^{m-1}\right]\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) for every negative integer \(n\).

blocks.prompt: 11 Show that \(f(x) = |x|\) is continuous at \(x = 0\) but not differentiable there. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Continuity: both one-sided limits of \(f\) equal \(f(0)\). Differentiability: the one-sided limits of \(\frac{|\delta x|}{\delta x}\) differ.

book_ref.quote: Now we check the differentiability of

steps: \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0^{+}}\dfrac{|\delta x|}{\delta x} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0^{+}}\dfrac{\delta x}{\delta x} = 1\)
\(\lim_{\delta x \to 0^{-}}\dfrac{|\delta x|}{\delta x} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0^{-}}\dfrac{-\delta x}{\delta x} = -1\)
The right-hand and left-hand limits are not equal, so \(f'(0) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{|\delta x|}{\delta x}\) does not exist.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(|x|\) is continuous at \(0\) but not differentiable there (no tangent at the corner).

blocks.prompt: 12 Let \(f(x) = |x - 1|\). Show that \(f\) is continuous at \(x = 1\) but \(f'(1)\) does not exist. Also find \(f'(x)\) for \(x > 1\) and for \(x < 1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Same method as for \(|x|\) at \(0\), with the corner at \(x = 1\).

book_ref.quote: A function can be continuous at a point but not necessarily differentiable there.

steps: Right-hand limit (\(\delta x \to 0^{+}\)) \(= 1\); left-hand limit (\(\delta x \to 0^{-}\)) \(= -1\). Not equal, so \(f'(1)\) does not exist.
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) is continuous at \(1\), \(f'(1)\) does not exist; \(f'(x) = 1\) for \(x > 1\) and \(f'(x) = -1\) for \(x < 1\).

blocks.prompt: 13 If \(c\) is a constant and \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), prove that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[cf(x)] = c\dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x)]\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the four steps on \(y = cf(x)\) and take the constant out of the limit.

book_ref.quote: A constant factor can be taken out from a limit sign.

steps: Let \(y = cf(x)\). Then \(y + \delta y = cf(x + \delta x)\)
\(\delta y = cf(x + \delta x) - cf(x) = c[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)]\)
\(\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = c\left[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\right]\)
\(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = c\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\) (a constant factor comes out of a limit)

blocks.prompt: 14 If \(f\) and \(g\) are differentiable at \(x\), prove that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x) + g(x)] = \dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x)] + \dfrac{d}{dx}[g(x)]\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Let \(\phi = f + g\); rearrange the change of \(\phi\) into the change of \(f\) plus the change of \(g\).

book_ref.quote: The limit of a sum is the sum of the limits

steps: Let \(\phi(x) = f(x) + g(x)\). Then \(\phi(x + \delta x) = f(x + \delta x) + g(x + \delta x)\)
\(\dfrac{\phi(x + \delta x) - \phi(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x} + \dfrac{g(x + \delta x) - g(x)}{\delta x}\)
Taking \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\) (the limit of a sum is the sum of the limits): \(\phi'(x) = f'(x) + g'(x)\)
The difference rule is proved the same way with \(\phi(x) = f(x) - g(x)\): \(\phi'(x) = f'(x) - g'(x)\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \([f(x) + g(x)]' = f'(x) + g'(x)\) (and \([f(x) - g(x)]' = f'(x) - g'(x)\)).

blocks.prompt: 15 If \(f\) and \(g\) are differentiable at \(x\), prove the product rule \([f(x)g(x)]' = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Subtract and add \(f(x)g(x + \delta x)\), then use the limit theorems and continuity of \(g\).

book_ref.quote: Subtracting and adding \(f(x)\,g(x + \delta x)\)

steps: Let \(\phi(x) = f(x)g(x)\). Then \(\phi(x + \delta x) - \phi(x) = f(x + \delta x)g(x + \delta x) - f(x)g(x)\)
Subtract and add \(f(x)g(x + \delta x)\): \(= [f(x + \delta x) - f(x)]g(x + \delta x) + f(x)[g(x + \delta x) - g(x)]\)
\(\dfrac{\phi(x + \delta x) - \phi(x)}{\delta x} = \left[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\right]g(x + \delta x) + f(x)\left[\dfrac{g(x + \delta x) - g(x)}{\delta x}\right]\)
Taking \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\) with the limit theorems: \(\phi'(x) = f'(x)\lim_{\delta x \to 0}g(x + \delta x) + f(x)g'(x)\)
Since \(g\) is differentiable it is continuous, so \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}g(x + \delta x) = g(x)\); thus \(\phi'(x) = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x)\)

blocks.prompt: 16 If \(f\) and \(g\) are differentiable at \(x\) and \(g(x) \ne 0\), prove the quotient rule \(\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)' = \dfrac{f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^{2}}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Take a common denominator, subtract and add \(f(x)g(x)\) in the numerator, divide by \(\delta x\) and take the limit.

book_ref.quote: Subtracting and adding \(f(x)g(x)\) in the numerator of step (ii) gives

steps: Let \(\phi(x) = \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\). Then \(\phi(x + \delta x) - \phi(x) = \dfrac{f(x + \delta x)g(x) - f(x)g(x + \delta x)}{g(x)g(x + \delta x)}\)
Subtract and add \(f(x)g(x)\) in the numerator: \(= \dfrac{1}{g(x)g(x + \delta x)}\Big[\big(f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\big)g(x) - f(x)\big(g(x + \delta x) - g(x)\big)\Big]\)
\(\dfrac{\phi(x + \delta x) - \phi(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{1}{g(x)g(x + \delta x)}\Big[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}g(x) - f(x)\dfrac{g(x + \delta x) - g(x)}{\delta x}\Big]\)
Taking \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\), using \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0}g(x + \delta x) = g(x)\): \(\phi'(x) = \dfrac{1}{g(x)\cdot g(x)}[f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)]\)

blocks.prompt: 17 Differentiate \(y = (x^{2} + 1)(x^{3} - 2x)\) with respect to \(x\) by the product rule, and verify the answer by multiplying out first. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Product rule with \(f = x^{2} + 1\), \(g = x^{3} - 2x\); then expand and use the sum rule.

book_ref.quote: If \(f\) and \(g\) are differentiable at \(x\), then \(fg\) is also differentiable

blocks.prompt: 18 Differentiate \(\dfrac{x^{2} - 3x + 1}{x^{2} + 2}\) with respect to \(x\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Quotient rule; \(x^{2} + 2 \ne 0\) for every real \(x\).

book_ref.quote: Unlike the product rule, the ORDER matters here because of the minus sign

blocks.prompt: 19 If \(y = \dfrac{x^{2} + 1}{x}\), \(x \ne 0\), find \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) by the quotient rule and show that \(x^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^{2} - 1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Quotient rule, then multiply by \(x^{2}\); check by writing \(y = x + x^{-1}\).

book_ref.quote: then \(\frac{f}{g}\) is differentiable at

blocks.prompt: 20 A firm's profit from \(x\) units is \(P(x) = 240x - 6x^{2} - 900\). (i) Find the marginal profit when \(x = 15\). (ii) Find the number of units that gives the largest profit and that profit. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Marginal profit \(= P'(x)\); the largest profit is where \(P'(x) = 0\) and \(P'\) changes from positive to negative.

book_ref.quote: the marginal profit is the derivative of the profit function with respect to

steps: \(P'(19) = 12 > 0\) and \(P'(21) = -12 < 0\): profit rises, then falls, so \(x = 20\) gives the largest profit.
blocks.final_answer: (i) Marginal profit \(60\) per unit at \(x = 15\). (ii) \(20\) units give the largest profit, \(1500\).

blocks.prompt: 21 A particle moves along a line with \(s(t) = 2t^{3} - 15t^{2} + 24t\) metres after \(t\) seconds. Find (i) the velocity and acceleration at \(t = 3\) s, (ii) the times when the particle is at rest. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(v = s'(t)\), \(a = v'(t)\); at rest means \(v = 0\).

book_ref.quote: velocity is the derivative of the position function, and acceleration is the derivative of the velocity function

blocks.prompt: 22 The cost of building a cylindrical tank of base radius \(r\) is \(C(r) = 2000\pi r^{2} + \dfrac{32000}{r}\), \(r > 0\). Find the radius that minimizes the cost and the least cost. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Set \(C'(r) = 0\), solve for \(r\) (cube root gives \(r\)), check the sign of \(C'\) on both sides.

book_ref.quote: at the lowest point of the cost curve the rate of change of cost is zero

steps: \(C'(1) = 4000\pi - 32000 < 0\), \(C'(2) = 8000\pi - 8000 > 0\): the cost falls, then rises, so this \(r\) gives the least cost.

blocks.prompt: 23 The value of an investment after \(t\) years is \(V(t) = 8000(1 + 0.05t)^{2}\) rupees. Find (i) the rate of change of its value after \(5\) years, (ii) its value after \(5\) years. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expand the square first so that only formulas 1 to 4 are needed.

book_ref.quote: the rate of change of the investment is the derivative of

blocks.prompt: 24 The stress on a beam is \(S(x) = 600x - 2x^{3}\) Pa at \(x\) metres from the fixed end. (i) Find the rate of change of stress at \(x = 5\) m and say whether the stress is increasing or decreasing there. (ii) Find where the stress is largest and the largest stress. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(S'(x)\) gives the rate; the largest stress is where \(S'(x) = 0\) with \(S'\) changing from positive to negative.

book_ref.quote: the rate of change of stress is the derivative of

steps: (i) \(S'(5) = 600 - 150 = 450\) Pa per metre; positive, so the stress is increasing at \(x = 5\) m.
blocks.final_answer: (i) \(450\) Pa per metre, increasing. (ii) Largest stress \(4000\) Pa at \(x = 10\) m.
